title: Wet Mount / Hanging Drop

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: To observe living, unstained microorganisms — particularly to assess true motility, general shape, and size — without the fixation or staining artifacts that can alter or kill cells.
principle: A drop of a liquid culture or suspension is placed on a slide (wet mount) or on a coverslip suspended over a depression slide (hanging drop) so cells remain alive and can be observed moving under the microscope, typically with reduced condenser light or phase contrast for better contrast.
requiredMaterials: Microscope slide (plain for wet mount, depression slide for hanging drop)
Petroleum jelly (hanging drop, to seal the coverslip edges and slow drying)
Compound brightfield microscope, ideally with reduced light or phase contrast

procedure.instruction: Wet mount: place a small drop of the culture/suspension on a plain slide, lower a coverslip at an angle to avoid trapping air bubbles.

Hanging drop: apply a thin ring of petroleum jelly around the depression on a depression slide, place a drop of culture on the center of a coverslip, then invert the depression slide onto the coverslip so the drop hangs into the depression, and press gently to seal.
Examine promptly under the microscope, starting at lower magnification, reducing the condenser aperture/light for contrast, then moving to higher power as needed.
Distinguish true motility (directed or tumbling movement powered by the cell) from Brownian motion (a passive, jittering vibration common to all small particles in suspension, including dead cells).

observations: Record cell shape, relative size, arrangement, and whether movement observed is true motility or Brownian motion.
interpretation: True motility supports (but does not alone confirm) identification narrowing, since motility varies by genus/species and can also depend on growth conditions and culture age.
precautions: Handle wet preparations of live cultures as potentially infectious; dispose of slides and coverslips per biosafety procedure.
Avoid confusing Brownian motion with true motility — this is the most common misinterpretation of this technique.
limitations: Unstained cells have low contrast under standard brightfield illumination; phase contrast or reduced-light technique is often needed to see them well.
Preparations dry out relatively quickly, limiting observation time (hanging drop slows this compared to a plain wet mount).
biosafetyNotes: Containment requirements depend on the organism, not the mounting technique.
